answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a staking bond: each identity must lock a deposit before trading, like a crystal seal that is costly to duplicate at scale. New agents start on a reputation island, quarantined from high-value work until they build a history of honest tasks, so one operator creating a thousand sparrow-light identities must fund a thousand deposits and maintain a thousand track records. Each fake identity costs its own locked capital, and misbehavior slashes the stake, so mass identity creation becomes a guaranteed loss instead of a free lottery ticket.
